subject: Audit & access logs — regional export options, TTL and deletion attestation

Subject: Request: full audit/access log export options + retention TTL

Hi Karthik —

We're preparing for an upcoming compliance review and need a clear write-up of Redwood's capabilities for audit/access log exports. Specifically:

- Retention periods you provide for tenant-level audit logs (what's stored by default vs. what can be extended)
- Export formats and whether exports include indexed metadata (actor IDs, IP, region, model version)
- Residency / regional constraints (can exports be restricted to US-only storage and egress?)
- Deletion attestation: if HealthSys requests deletion of logs older than X days, can Redwood provide a signed attestation or proof-of-erasure?

Can you provide a short Q&A and example timeline for producing a bulk export for a single tenant (size estimate per month, typical SLA for delivery, and delivery modes e.g., signed URL vs. SFTP)?

Thanks — this is time-sensitive for our audit window next month.

— Priya (HealthSys audits)

Subject: Re: Request: full audit/access log export options + retention TTL

Hi all —

Quick technical summary to answer the three bullets Priya listed:

- Retention: By default tenant audit/access logs are retained 90 days in 'hot' indexed storage. Customers can request retention extensions up to 7 years via a Reserved Evidence package (long-term cold slice) — that moves events to an indexed archive stored in encrypted blobs. Extension requires a contractual add-on (monthly/annual).

- Export formats & metadata: Exports are provided as newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) and as compressed CSV for smaller payloads. Both include the canonical fields: timestamp, event_type, actor_id (internal UUID), actor_email (when available), source_ip, region, resource_id, model_version, request_id, and full raw_payload for the event (if requested). We can optionally include session identifiers and request headers for forensic needs.

- Residency / egress: We support regional egress controls. For US-only residency you can request exports from a US region-only export node; the delivery mechanism can be a pre-signed URL to a US-hosted S3 bucket (we will not egress across borders in that flow). We also support SFTP and customer-managed pull using temporary credentials for on-prem deliveries.

- Deletion attestation: For standard deletion we provide a signed deletion receipt (SHA256 manifest + timestamp + Redwood-signed key) showing objects removed from the archive slice and the tombstone workflow that removed index references. For customers that require an independent attestation (e.g., for legal hold release), we can provide our internal deletion playbook + deletion logs and a signed certificate (subject to legal review and possible additional fees).

Sizing & SLA (examples):
- Typical monthly tenant export (audit + access, medium activity): 8–30 GB compressed (ndjson gz)
- SLA for export creation: standard queue 5 business days; expedited (1–3 business days) for priority customers with reserved capacity. Delivery via URL/SFTP once prepared.

I attached a sample schema and a runbook draft (audit_log_schema_v2.csv, export_runbook_draft.pdf).

Happy to run a sample extract to show fields.

Best,
Marissa
Product Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachments: audit_log_schema_v2.csv (schema stub), export_runbook_draft.pdf (runbook draft)

Folks —

A couple of legal/contract points for HealthSys to consider:

- Retention add-ons (the Reserved Evidence package) require an amendment to the Master Subscription Agreement. Lead time for provisioning archive slices is typically 7–10 business days after signature.
- Deletion attestation: we can provide a Redwood-signed certificate of erasure for archived blobs and a manifest of removed object IDs. For GDPR/DSAR style proof-of-erasure, we recommend coupling our attestation with the customer's internal log purge (we can provide the manifest for their records).
- Cross-border restrictions: if HealthSys needs strict US-only export, ensure the purchase order references US regional egress; that avoids default multi-region failover during extreme incidents.

I'll prepare short contract language HealthSys can include in their PO to speed procurement if they choose the retention extension.

— Neha
Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference
